# [Julia Programming Language]{.flow} {.title}

## Why Julia?

- **Designed to be:**   
    - as general as Python
    - as statistics-friendly as R
    - as fast as C++!


:::{.callout-tip}
**Allows for fast data workflows**, particularly in scientific computing!
:::

## Syntax

- Dynamically-typed syntax just like Python
- Similar to R, Matlab and Python - **not like C++**
- In comparison, accessible and easy to learn!
- **No need to worry about memory management!**

## JuMP

- Package for **algebraic modeling** in Julia
- Simplifies solving complex optimization problems
- Provides a high-level, user-friendly interface
- Useful for operations research and data science

:::{.callout-tip}
JuMP is an alternative to Pyomo, GAMS, and AMPL!
:::

# [Algebraic Modeling]{.flow} {.title}

## What is algebraic modeling?

- A "mathematical language" for optimization problems
- Allows for describing complex systems and constraints
- Based on linear algebra (Equations and Inequalities)

## How to learn algebraic modeling?

- **Practice, practice, and practice!**
- Understand standard models and their approach
- Develop an understanding of constraints
- Understand the structure of a models solution space
- Use an available algorithms to determine solutions

## Central Questions

- What is to be decided?
- What is relevant to the decision?
- What information is given and relevant?
- What parameters (data) are needed?
- Which variables and of which type are needed?

:::{.callout-tip}
Modeling is a creative process!
:::

## Model Components

1. Objective function
2. Constraints
3. Variables

## Linear Optimization Model

#### Basic Model Formulation

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{maximize} \quad F = \sum_{j\in \mathcal{J}} c_j \times X_j
\end{aligned}
$$

subject to

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\sum_{j\in \mathcal{J}} a_{i,j} \times X_j  \le b_i && \forall i \in \mathcal{I} \\
&X_j \ge 0 &&  \forall  j \in \mathcal{J} 
\end{aligned}
$$

#### Model Components

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal{I} &: \text{set of $i \in \mathcal{I}$,}\\
\mathcal{J} &: \text{set of $j \in \mathcal{J}$,}\\
F 	&: \text{Objective function variable,}\\
X_{j}	&: \text{decision variables,}\\
c_{j}	&: \text{objective function coefficients,}\\
a_{i,j}	&: \text{parameters,}\\
b_{i}	&: \text{parameters}
\end{aligned}
$$

## What is modelling good for?

- [Good Question!]{.highlight} A lot of things:
    - Modeling real-world problems
    - Solving complex systems
    - Optimizing resource allocation
    - Decision-making under constraints
    - Simulation and prediction

# [Installing Julia]{.flow} {.title}

## Download and Install Julia

To prepare for the upcoming lectures, we start by installing the Julia Programming Language and an Integrated Development Environment (IDE) to work with Julia.

## Installing Julia

![](https://images.beyondsimulations.com/ao/ao_julia2.png){max-width=400px fig-alt="Screenshot of the julialang.org homepage, headed The Julia Programming Language, with a green Download button next to a Documentation button."}

- Head to [julialang.org](https://julialang.org) and follow the instructions.
- The easiest way to install Julia is via the shell/terminal
- Later, you can then manage Julia with `juliaup`

:::{.callout-tip}
If you are ever asked to add something to your "PATH", do so!
:::

## Zed

- Next, we are going to install [Zed](https://zed.dev), the editor of this workshop
- macOS: `brew install --cask zed` (or the installer from [zed.dev](https://zed.dev))
- Windows: installer from [zed.dev/windows](https://zed.dev/windows)
- Linux: `curl -f https://zed.dev/install.sh | sh`

:::{.callout-tip}
On Windows, Zed needs a DirectX-11-capable GPU. If it only shows a blank window, use [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com) with the "Julia (Julia Language Support)" extension instead: everything in this workshop works there too.
:::

## Verify the Installation

- Start Zed and take a look around
- Open the command palette: `Ctrl+Shift+P` (Windows/Linux) or `Cmd+Shift+P` (macOS)
- Choose **zed: extensions** and search for "Julia"
- Install the Julia extension for syntax support

## Create a new file

- Create a new file with a ".jl" ending
- Save it somewhere on your computer
- e.g., in a folder that you will use in the course

```{julia}
#| eval: true
#| output-location: fragment
print("Hello World!")
```

- Open a terminal in that folder and run the file with:
- `julia test.jl`

## Everything working?

- If the terminal prints `Hello World!` → perfect!
- If not, the terminal likely [cannot find the path]{.highlight} to Julia
- Close and reopen the terminal after installing Julia, and say yes to any "PATH" question during installation
- Then try to run the file again

## Installation Checklist

Before you start with the first tutorial, make sure you can:

- [ ] Open Zed
- [ ] See the Julia extension installed in **zed: extensions**
- [ ] Create a new `.jl` file
- [ ] See syntax highlighting in your Julia file
- [ ] Run code and see output in the terminal

## How to get started?

- Following three parts are dedicated to learning the basics
- Start with the very basics and gradually move on
- Focus in the first two parts on the programming language
- Third part dedicated to [Mathematical Optimization]{.highlight}

# [Julia in Zed]{.flow} {.title}

## Tutorials in Zed

- The easiest way to work on the tutorials is a `.jl` file in Zed, run cell by cell
- For detailed instructions, just open the [first tutorial](part-01/tutorial-01-01-variables.qmd)
- It explains step-by-step how to set up the workshop environment and run the cells

## Downloading the Files

- You will find the tutorial files next to the sections pages
- On each page, you will find a link `Julia` on the right (under "Code Links")
- Click it to download the `.jl` file and save it
- Prefer a notebook? The link `Jupyter` (under "Other Formats") downloads the same tutorial as `.ipynb`
- I'd recommend storing the files [in a separate directory for this workshop]{.highlight}

## Get started with the sections

- Download the first `.jl` file and open it in Zed
- Start with the [first problem and solve it step by step]{.highlight}
- You can find the sections here on the website
- [You can ask questions anytime!]{.highlight}
